title: Am I Buying the Dip in Broadcom Stock? | AVGO Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate asks whether Broadcom (AVGO) is a buying opportunity after management reiterated it can double AI revenue from $115B next year to over $230B by 2027, even in a supply-constrained environment for data centres, power and chips — and that without constraints revenue would be significantly higher. The mix is shifting toward the lower-margin semiconductor segment, but operating margins should still rise on scale. Wall Street expects earnings per share to grow over 54% a year for the next several years, up from just 15% in 2024. He highlights faster product delivery — the custom OpenAI ASIC, codenamed Jalapeno, shipped in under 10 months — and management credibility: after the VMware deal, operating margins fell as promised, then recovered to 48.6% over the trailing twelve months, above the pre-deal peak. The balance sheet has improved markedly, with cash and short-term investments over $23.9B and long-term debt under $60B, roughly $20B of debt paid down and ~$14B of cash added from operations. Despite all the positives, the stock trades at a forward P/E of just 9.65, the cheapest in years and about a fifth of its EPS growth rate, and his DCF fair value is $462 against a $293 market price, over 50% upside. He reiterates his BUY with high conviction, owns the stock and wants to add more. Call: AVGO BUY reiterated, high conviction. He flags Nvidia's 17 November earnings as a major event for all investors.
